session_note: Hawaii runs two-year bienniums (2023-2024, 2025-2026); a bill introduced in the first year that has not passed by the end of that year's session is automatically carried over into the second year of the SAME biennium (marked with a 'Carried over to [year] Regular Session' housekeeping entry on the bill-status page), but any bill that has not passed both chambers by the end of the second year dies with the biennium and does not carry into the next biennium (confirmed directly on capitol.hawaii.gov's own measure-status pages for SB284 and SB338 below). Resolutions (HR/SR/HCR/SCR) are generally introduced fresh each year and do not carry the same multi-year life as bills. The 2026 regular session convened the third Wednesday in January (2026-01-21) per the state constitution's 60-working-day limit; I could not independently fetch a dedicated 'session calendar/deadlines' page confirming an official sine die date (capitol.hawaii.gov returned 403/404 for the calendar URLs tried and the web-search tool's quota was exhausted for this session), but the bill-status pages themselves show floor action concluding by 2026-04-27 (HCR206 final adoption) with only post-adjournment ministerial entries after that (e.g. SR90 'Certified copies of resolutions sent' on 2026-05-12), consistent with Hawaii's typical late-April/early-May sine die pattern in recent years.

decisions.notes: This packet entry bundles two companion Senate measures with different final dispositions, so a single bill_status_category cannot capture both exactly; passed_one_chamber is used to reflect that at least one of the two (SR90) reached final adoption, while SCR95's fate (died in House committee, concurrent resolution never adopted by the House) is spelled out in the status text. This clarifies and goes beyond the packet's snapshot ('SCR95 referred to House EEP/FIN on 2026-04-10; SR90 SD1 text available'), which did not state whether either measure was ultimately adopted - hence outcome status_changed. Since the 2026 session has concluded (see session_note) with no further House action on SCR95, and resolutions do not carry over the way bills do, SCR95 is dead for this biennium.
